title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover and load-shedding
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent thrashing during regional failover and load-shedding. Includes guardrails and additional telemetry.
description: Context: During a regional capacity loss incident we observed the SLO enforcer enter a backoff ordering race that caused repeated rapid failovers and aggressive load-shedding across regions. This made recovery unstable and increased customer-visible error rates. Root cause: an ordering race between the regional failover coordinator and the SLO enforcer backoff state machine 1 concurrent backoff updates could be applied out-of-order when nodes recovered and rejoined, which temporarily pushed healthy regions into higher backoff tiers and triggered load-shedding loops. Impact: user request error rates spiked in affected customers, latency SLOs violated for several minutes during failover windows. This PR contains a hotfix to make backoff updates idempotent, add ordering stamps, and add a conservative hysteresis window for regional backoff transitions to prevent thrash during load-shedding windows. Changes: - Add monotonic backoff_epoch with compare-and-apply semantics in SLO enforcer control plane. - Introduce a 15s hysteresis window before applying a lower-priority backoff (prevents immediate downgrade after transient recovery). - Ensure regional failover coordinator tags failover decisions with coordinator epoch and the enforcer rejects stale epochs. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate node rejoin and concurrent backoff updates. - Add additional metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_applied, slo_enforcer.backoff_rejected_stale, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_skipped. - Update documentation (runtime/ops) with recommended hysteresis defaults and guidance for emergency rollbacks. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced race in perf-canary harness - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test (regional failover scenario) added - [x] E2E smoke in staging - [x] Rollout/rollback plan documented Testing & validation: ran integration scenario that simulates a regional outage with 3 region controllers; validated that only the intended region transitions to higher backoff, that recovered regions respect hysteresis and do not immediately trigger load-shedding, and that metrics show reduced backoff thrash. Rollout plan: - Canary to 5% of traffic in non-critical region group for 2 hours - Monitor slo_enforcer.* metrics, request_error_rate, and regional failover alarms - If stable -> gradual 25% -> 100% across regions Emergency rollback: revert to previous enforcer image (tag v2026.02.15) and set slo_enforcer.hysteresis_override=true via console if needed. Notes: this is intentionally conservative (15s hysteresis) to avoid user-visible latency regressions while preventing thrash; we can tune after observing production telemetry. Related: ENG-7123 tracks long-term fix to unify coordinator/enforcer state machine; SUP-2311 is the customer impact ticket.

review_comments: Evan Cooper: Can you add a short explanation of why 15s was chosen? It seems conservative but we should document reason.
Priya Nair: 15s chosen based on historical recovery windows from recent incidents (median ~8s, 95th ~40s); we bias conservative for safety and will tune post-rollout.
Luis Chen: r=me after tests added and one extra metric for rejected stale writes
Priya Nair: added slo_enforcer.backoff_rejected_stale and updated tests to assert metric emission

notes: Post-merge: created a follow-up ENG ticket to remove hysteresis or make it configurable per-customer after 1 week of telemetry: ENG-7199. Ops notified via #sre-oncall and pagerduty runbook updated.

rollback_instructions: To rollback: redeploy slo-enforcer image to tag v2026.02.15 and set slo_enforcer.hysteresis_override=true. Watch slo_enforcer.* metrics and request_error_rate for 15 minutes.
